newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds surrender gains at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds surrender gains at close.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed flat to lower Wednesday, erasing strong early gains on the back of a slight uptick in U.S. long bond yields.

"The market rallied at the opening and reached record levels, but then it stalled and gave back gains," a trader at a leading foreign bank said. "The reversal reflected movements in U.S. Treasuries, but you can also blame it on normal profit-taking."
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 shed 1/4 to 94-5/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 dropped $0.42 to 118.0.
Dealers said the market was regrouping after posting strong gains Tuesday on the back U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's congressional testimony.

"Greenspan's words have ratified the prevailing bullish mood on the markets. But prices first need to consolidate at these high levels, so I don't expect any major price movements near term," another dealer said.
Greenspan forecast in congressional testimony this week that economic growth would slow down and inflation would not accelerate despite current low unemployment levels.
